hero.lead: A nation of 623,000 between the mountains and the Adriatic, with forest across six tenths of its land and €383.5 million earmarked under the EU Growth Plan.

capital.heading: Mountains, coast and reforms, and only treated water.

record.text: Preliminary allocation under the EU Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans, 2024-2027
Received under the Growth Plan by August 2026
First Resilient Fiscal and Sustainable Development DPF, October 2024
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025
Gross public debt at the end of September 2025, 58.59% of estimated GDP

register.name: Seven-year Eurobond (4.875%)
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued at the beginning of April 2025 · seven-year maturity · coupon 4.875%
register.note: Raised to repay obligations incurred earlier, not to finance current spending
register.text: An €850 million seven-year bond of Montenegro on international markets at a coupon of 4.875%, used to repay debt falling due. It refinances the public finances as a whole; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Waste Management Reform Project
register.detail: World Bank · P510187 · approved 27 March 2026 · Regional Waste Management Center in Nikšić · remediation of about 11 hectares at the former KAP site
register.note: The Nikšić center will serve more than 75,000 people
register.text: A World Bank loan to strengthen solid waste management, financing a regional center in Nikšić for recycling, composting and modern waste treatment, so that less waste goes to landfill, and the clean-up of contaminated land at the former KAP site. Cleaner waste services serve the shelter and health standards, where sanitation is furthest from reach.

register.name: Forests for Shared Prosperity Project
register.detail: World Bank · P507869 · approved 18 March 2026 · sustainable forest management, wildfire risk and wood processing
register.note: Expected outcomes include job creation and a better quality of life
register.text: A World Bank loan for more sustainable forest management, a lower risk of wildfires and the growth of wood-processing businesses and their jobs. Forests support rural incomes, so the project serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Climate Resilient Fisheries and Agrifood Sector Development Project
register.detail: World Bank · P507698 · approved 17 December 2025 · €33 million ($38.76 million) · port services for fishers and a Paying Agency closer to farmers
register.note: Helps fishers reach higher-value markets and aligns the sector with EU rules
register.text: A World Bank loan to strengthen fisheries and the agrifood sector, key pillars of the economy, by improving services, modernising infrastructure and ensuring EU compliance. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Financial Infrastructure Modernization and SEPA Alignment
register.detail: World Bank · P509405 · approved 28 July 2025 · fast payments through the TIPS clone solution
register.note: Aims to reach an additional 110,000 people, 70,000 of them women; about 15% of the population is unbanked
register.text: A World Bank loan to modernise the digital payments infrastructure, lower the cost of domestic and international transactions and align Montenegro with the Single Euro Payments Area. Wider access to accounts and cheaper payments serve the livelihood standard.

register.name: Energy Sector Decarbonization Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 4 December 2024
register.text: Cleaner power and energy efficiency.
register.note: World Bank project P505964

register.name: First Resilient Fiscal and Sustainable Development DPF
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 4 October 2024
register.text: Budget support for fiscal and sustainable development reforms.
register.note: World Bank project P178646

register.name: Reform and Growth Facility (EU Growth Plan)
register.detail: European Commission · Reform Agenda approved October 2024 · pre-financing of €26.8 million · €44.2 million released on 20 May 2026
register.text: Grants and concessional loans from the EU paid against reform steps completed under Montenegro’s Reform Agenda, up to €383 million by 2027. Of the €44.2 million released on 20 May 2026, €20.6 million went to the state budget and the rest to investment projects through the Western Balkans Investment Framework, which also carried the energy infrastructure part of the pre-financing. It supports the public finances as a whole and the energy standard.
register.note: The Facility has an envelope of €6 billion for the Western Balkans; Montenegro had received €89.3 million by 20 May 2026

register.name: Credit lines for SMEs in renewable energy and energy efficiency
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 11 May 2026 · loan to the Development Bank of Montenegro
register.note: One of the operations signed on 11 May 2026, worth more than €250 million in all
register.text: An EIB loan to the Development Bank of Montenegro for new credit lines to small and medium-sized enterprises that carry out renewable energy and energy efficiency projects. It serves the energy and livelihood standards and the energy security of the country.

register.name: Equipping healthcare facilities in Montenegro
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20250290 · signed 22 April 2026 · total cost €115 million · loan to the Ministry of Health, launched on 11 May 2026
register.note: New medical technology for more than 30 public hospitals and clinics
register.text: An EIB loan within a €115 million programme that includes a new general hospital in Pljevlja, a new health centre in Podgorica, a haematology clinic at the Clinical Center of Montenegro and upgraded medical equipment for more than 30 public healthcare institutions. It serves the health standard.

register.name: 220 kV transmission line to Albania and Bosnia and Herzegovina
register.detail: EBRD · EBRD news, 2026 · loan to Crnogorski elektroprenosni sistem (CGES) · guarantee from the Ministry of Finance
register.note: Up to €15 million; expected to roughly double the corridor’s capacity to about 600 MW
register.text: An EBRD loan to the national transmission operator to upgrade a 220 kV overhead line linking Montenegro with Albania and Bosnia and Herzegovina. A stronger grid serves the energy standard and the integration of renewable power.

register.name: Healthcare system loan
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 5 April 2025 · signed 17 October 2025 · in support of the Health Strategy 2023–2027
register.note: Expected to meet the needs of 250,000 patients
register.text: A CEB loan to Montenegro for a new general hospital in Pljevlja, a health centre in the City Quart area of Podgorica, a haematology clinic at the Clinical Centre of Montenegro and MRI, CT and PET-CT scanners. It targets vulnerable and underserved groups, among them low-income households, rural communities, displaced persons and persons with disabilities, and serves the health standard.

register.name: Gvozd wind farm expansion
register.detail: EBRD · committed in 2025 · additional loan for three turbines · developed by Elektroprivreda Crne Gore (EPCG) and its subsidiaries · first loan signed in 2023
register.note: Capacity rises from 55 MW to 75 MW, enough for more than 35,000 households
register.text: An additional EBRD loan for three more wind turbines at Gvozd, the wind farm of the national power utility, with full commissioning expected by the end of 2026. It adds clean generation and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Digitalisation of the electricity distribution system
register.detail: EBRD · committed in 2025 · national electricity distribution system
register.note: One of 18 EBRD projects in Montenegro in 2025, worth €215 million in all
register.text: An EBRD loan for the digitalisation of the national electricity distribution system, for greater reliability and safety and the integration of renewable energy. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Water supply and wastewater in Kolašin, Rožaje and Mojkovac
register.detail: EIB Global · EU grant through the Western Balkans Investment Framework · signed 10 March 2025 in Podgorica · with a €10 million EIB loan signed earlier
register.note: For about 30,000 people; the same page also gives the grant as €22.5 million
register.text: An EU grant agreement, signed with EIB Global and the Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Northern Region Development, for sustainable water supply and wastewater systems in three northern municipalities. It serves the water and shelter standards; shelter, measured by safely managed sanitation, is the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Modernisation of the Perućica and Pljevlja 2 substations
register.detail: Agence Française de Développement · signed 28 July 2026 · sovereign-guaranteed loan to CGES · guarantee agreement signed by the Minister of Finance
register.note: A planned €8.5 million grant from the Western Balkans Investment Framework is part of the financing plan
register.text: An AFD loan to the national transmission operator to modernise two substations; the Perućica upgrade will allow up to 350 MW of hydropower into the grid and Pljevlja 2 reinforces trans-Balkan links. It serves the energy standard and the gradual move away from coal.

register.name: Development Policy Loan, second tranche
register.detail: Agence Française de Développement · signed 4 June 2026 in Cetinje by the Minister of Finance · structured in partnership with the World Bank
register.note: An AFD grant of up to €290,000 for the distribution operator CEDIS was signed the same day
register.text: Budget support from France for reforms in waste management, renewable energy, sustainable forestry, pollution reduction and climate resilience, linked to Chapter 27 of the EU accession negotiations. It supports the public finances as a whole and reforms that serve the energy standard.

register.name: Ulcinj wastewater treatment plant
register.detail: KfW and the European Union · WBIF grant agreement signed 16 October 2025 · works began 17 October 2025 · EU grant of €31 million · KfW loan of over €26 million · national contributions
register.note: Capacity of 60,000 population equivalent; it will end the discharge of untreated effluent into the Adriatic Sea
register.text: The total estimated investment in a wastewater treatment plant for Ulcinj, financed by an EU grant through the Western Balkans Investment Framework, a KfW loan and national contributions. It serves the shelter standard, measured by safely managed sanitation, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Energy efficiency in public buildings
register.detail: KfW and the European Union · WBIF news of 11 September 2025 · KfW loan of €45 million · EU grant of nearly €4.8 million · elementary schools in Berane and Bijelo Polje
register.note: Part of the Promotion of Energy Efficiency in Public Buildings programme
register.text: A KfW loan, with an EU grant through the Western Balkans Investment Framework, for energy efficiency upgrades to public buildings, among them three elementary schools in Berane and Bijelo Polje. Energy-efficient schools serve the education and energy standards.

register.name: Development Policy Loan for environment and climate reforms, 2024
register.detail: Agence Française de Développement · concluded with the Ministry of Finance in 2024
register.note: Complemented by the €100 million second tranche of June 2026
register.text: Budget support from France concluded in 2024 for reforms in environmental protection and climate change. It supports the public finances as a whole.

register.name: Loans for SMEs, women, youth and homes, NLB Banka Podgorica
register.detail: EBRD · 3 June 2026 · four senior unsecured loans: SMEs €7 million, Women in Business €2 million, Youth in Business €2 million, mortgages €7 million · EU support through EFSD+
register.note: A share is expected to fund energy-efficient investments and green mortgages
register.text: An EBRD package to NLB Banka Podgorica for loans to small businesses, to women- and youth-led businesses and for long-term residential mortgages, partly backed by EU risk-sharing instruments. It serves the livelihood and shelter standards.

register.name: Go Digital loan, Addiko Bank Podgorica
register.detail: EBRD · 26 February 2026 · Go Digital in the Western Balkans · EU grant incentives of 10% of sub-loans and technical assistance through the WBIF
register.note: Up to €2 million; open to women-led businesses
register.text: An EBRD loan to Addiko Bank Podgorica for small and medium-sized enterprises investing in digitalisation, green technologies and competitiveness. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loan to MFI Alter Modus for micro-enterprises
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 5 April 2025 · co-finances the loan portfolio of the borrower · supporting jobs and economic and financial inclusion
register.note: For micro-entrepreneurs, micro-enterprises and farmers
register.text: A CEB loan to Alter Modus, a microfinance institution, to co-finance its lending to entrepreneurs, micro-enterprises and farmers in Montenegro. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Green loans for SMEs and homes, CKB
register.detail: EBRD · 13 March 2025 · up to €7 million for SMEs and up to €5 million for homeowners · grant incentives from the EU and Japan
register.note: Homeowners can receive cashback grants of up to 20% of the loan value
register.text: An EBRD loan to Crnogorska Komercijalna Banka, the largest bank in the country, for green investments by small businesses and for thermal insulation and other green technologies in homes. It serves the energy, shelter and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Visitors already pay for the coast and the culture; their spending can finance what lasts.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Seljak.me
items.text: A web and mobile e-marketplace that links Montenegrin farmers with consumers, free to list on and funded by advertising rather than commissions on sales, with about 20,000 registered farmers and some 692,000 users between June 2025 and June 2026.

items.name: Alter Modus
items.text: A microfinance institution that lends to entrepreneurs, micro-enterprises and farmers in Montenegro, for which the Council of Europe Development Bank approved a €10 million loan in April 2025 to co-finance its loan portfolio.

items.name: Mondo Bianco
items.text: A laundry founded as a social enterprise by Caritas Bar, alongside its Script print shop and Most toy workshop, that trains and employs people with disabilities.

items.name: Nova šansa
items.text: A non-profit in Herceg Novi that runs a digital printing business with vocational training, financed partly by its own service income.

items.name: Zračak Nade
items.text: An association of parents of children with developmental disabilities in Pljevlja that runs a printing service to train and employ people with disabilities.

items.name: Association for Assistance to Persons with Mental and Physical Disabilities, Nikšić
items.text: An association in Nikšić that earns income for its work with people with mental and physical disabilities by selling decorative items and souvenirs and through its hair salon, Status.

coverage.gap_text: Of Montenegrins lack safely managed sanitation.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 10.4% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 8.8% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 73% cook with clean fuels and technology; 100% have electricity

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 84.2% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above the national poverty line; 20% live below it
